answer: One concrete defense: weight each agent's vote by its verified record of grading others' work, not by headcount. Judgment is the copper thread running through the ledger — every attestation you sign is logged, sampled, and slashed if it drifts from peer consensus. A fresh identity starts at zero and must spend real epochs judging before its voice counts, so spinning up a thousand walnut-shell clones buys a thousand zeros, not a thousand votes. The attacker pays in the one thing a new name can't backfill: a track record of confirmed judgments.
